human_tolerance.notes: Occupies a wide range of habitats including agricultural fields and urban areas, and may nest on man-made structures; huntfields and the open ground around them supply the rodents it needs.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Pairs construct a stick nest in a large tree 4-21 m up, or on a cliff ledge or man-made structure, 71-97 cm across; a clutch of one to five eggs is laid in spring.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: Nestlings emerge 42-46 days after hatching; fledging, including learning to hunt, takes about 10 weeks.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Wintering birds tend to be territorial and shift range when food requires it; some northern and coastal populations do not migrate at all.

vocalizations.description: A two- to three-second hoarse rasping scream, described as kree-eee-ar, that begins high and slurs downward, like a steam whistle; given while hunting or soaring and loudest in annoyance or anger.
A croaking guh-runk at close range; young hawks give a wailing klee-uk food cry when parents leave the nest.

range.note: Breeds from central Alaska and northern Canada south to Florida, the West Indies and Central America, down to Panama.

traits.limb_count.note: A bird: two legs are the limbs.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Soars and glides on broad wings; walks on the ground when hunting ground prey and perches in trees.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The pair constructs a stick nest in a high tree ... or on a cliff ledge ... or may nest on man-made structures' - a platform.

traits.perching.note: Perches conspicuously in trees and on poles.

traits.size_class.note: Derived from mass_kg (1.15 kg is in the Medium band).

traits.mass_kg.note: 'typically weighing from 690 to 1,600 g'; 1.15 kg is the midpoint.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Males 690-1,300 g and females 900-2,000 g; the 690-1,600 g headline range is used.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of the 105-141 cm standard measurement.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Judgement: no openly licensed source consulted states a wild lifespan for this species, and the article gives only sexual maturity at two years. Twelve years is an authored estimate for a large accipitrid, not a sourced figure.

traits.diet.note: 'Prey ... usually centers on rodents, comprising up to 85% of a hawk's diet', plus birds, reptiles and amphibians; carrion is eaten but not preferred.

traits.social.note: 'Pairs stay together for life, taking a new mate only when the original mate dies.'

traits.activity_pattern.note: A diurnal raptor that hunts from the air and perches to watch for prey.

traits.defense.note: Vocalises loudest in annoyance or anger at a predator or a rival hawk intruding into its territory; Mob recorded.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: wary of people and of disturbance near the nest, though it readily uses cities and man-made structures.

habitat.use.note: Most of the time is spent soaring and hunting from the air, with tree perches and occasional ground-level hunting; 60/30/10 is a judgement informed by EltonTraits.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Roosts and watches for prey from high perches in trees.

habitat.resources.note: Prey from the diet section; nest_platform and perch from the nesting section.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Occupies urban areas and nests on man-made structures, but needs open hunting ground; numeric tolerances authored.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'The species is a partial migrant, as in most of their range in Canada and Alaska, they almost entirely vacate their breeding grounds.'

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: Derived from the partial-migrant statement, which also notes that some northern and coastal populations do not migrate; 0.8 is a judgement for the overwintering share.

seasonal.phases.note: Spring stick-nest construction and a one-to-five-egg clutch, a 10-week nestling period, and winter territoriality from the Reproduction and Feeding sections.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg, altricial nestling and adult, with the sourced nestling and fledging intervals in the notes.

look.note: Adult: brown above with a paler streaked breast, a uniformly brick-red tail, yellow cere and legs, broad rounded wings; proportions authored (judgement).

behavior.note: Authored parameters for this species' own fsm-perching-raptor-v1 program: a 25 m perch horizon, a 60 m hunt range and a 150 m flush distance.
